title: Raising a Glass for National Beer Day
main_content:
April 7 was National Beer Day in the United States.

National Beer Day is not a real holiday.

But a lot of Americans are celebrating on social media.

One Twitter user wrote, “I hear it’s #NationalBeerDay and I feel fortunate to live where they make so much of it.”

The magazine Men’s Journal published a list of what it called the “100 Best Beers in America.”

Some of the beers have unusual names, such as Sloth, Fuzzy Baby Ducks and Lizard King.

April 7 is an important day in beer history. On that day in 1933, Americans could legally buy beer again after 13 years.

The 18th Amendment to the constitution took effect in 1920. It prohibited “the manufacture, sale or transportation of liquors.”

In December 1933, the 21st Amendment to the constitution officially ended prohibition. But a few months before that, President Franklin Roosevelt signed an act to permit the sale of low-alcohol wine and beer. That was on April 7.

questions.question: Is National Beer Day a real holiday?
options: No, it is not a real holiday.
No, but it is widely celebrated.
questions.answer: No, it is not a real holiday.

questions.question: Which magazine published “100 Best Beers in America” on National Beer Day?
Why is National Beer Day celebrated on April 7?
options: To commemorate the signing of the 21st Amendment.
It marks the day beer became legal again after prohibition.
To celebrate the invention of beer in America.
It is the birthday of a famous brewer.
questions.answer: It marks the day beer became legal again after prohibition.
